plan: With uniform values on [0,49] and 3 bidders in a first-price sealed-bid auction, the Bayesian Nash equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which accounts for competition while maximizing expected profit. With n=3 bidders, this means bidding 2/3 of my value. My value is $25, so I should bid approximately $16.7 to balance winning probability against profit margin.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, i.e., 2/3 * value. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. My value is $17, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 * 17 ≈ $11.30 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction bid strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which for n=3 is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $39, so bidding around $26 maximizes expected profit by accounting for competition from Andy and Betty while still capturing surplus if I win.
